name: The rmic static stub compiler was removed in JDK 15, breaking the Ant rmic task
description: The RMI static stub compiler rmic was deprecated for removal in JDK 13 and removed in JDK 15. JADE's build.xml calls Ant's <rmic> task twice at the end of the 'jade' target to pregenerate JRMP stubs for jade.imtp.rmi.ServiceManagerRMIImpl and jade.imtp.rmi.NodeRMIImpl. On a JDK 17 toolchain Ant refuses the task outright with 'rmic does not exist under Java 15 and higher', so the build stops after javac has already succeeded. This is the only change in the 11-to-17 window that stops the JADE build; everything else in this manifest compiles. Both implementation classes extend java.rmi.server.UnicastRemoteObject, which has generated stubs dynamically since Java 5, so deleting the two pregeneration steps removes a build dependency without removing a runtime capability.

blast_class_evidence.reason: Both sites are standalone <rmic/> elements inside the 'jade' Ant target. Deleting them changes no Java declaration, no Ant property and no other target's dependency list, so nothing outside the enclosing target has to be edited.

witnesses.note: jade.imtp.rmi.ServiceManagerRMIImpl extends UnicastRemoteObject (ServiceManagerRMIImpl.java:46); dynamic stubs replace the static ones

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: If a consumer loads a pregenerated *_Stub class by name instead of letting UnicastRemoteObject export the object, dynamic stubs will not cover it and the recipe must stop and report rather than delete.

patterns.reason: Ant <rmic> task; the rmic tool it drives was removed in JDK 15 and Ant refuses the task on JDK 15+

verification_hint: No build file in the workspace contains an <rmic element. 'ant clean lib' inside jade-ant:17 prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL and exits 0, and lib/jade.jar is produced. All consumers still PASS.

name: Primitive wrapper constructors deprecated for removal in JDK 16
description: JEP 390 (JDK 16) designated the primitive wrapper classes as value-based and deprecated their constructors for removal. Compiling JADE on JDK 17 with -Xlint:removal produces 144 removal warnings for new Boolean/Integer/Long/Double/Float/Character calls -- the single largest terminally-deprecated surface in the codebase. The code still compiles and runs on 17; the exposure is that these constructors are the ones scheduled to disappear. The fix is the documented replacement, the corresponding valueOf factory.

blast_class_evidence.reason: Every hit is an expression inside a method body, field initializer or argument list. new Integer(x) and Integer.valueOf(x) have the same static type, so no field type, method signature or return type changes and no caller outside the enclosing declaration is affected.

witnesses.note: argument to java.util.Stack.push(Object); the parameter type stays Object either way
value stored into an Object-typed slot of an abstract descriptor; declared types unchanged
Boolean.valueOf returns the interned TRUE/FALSE instances; see escalation_condition

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: valueOf may return a cached, shared instance where the constructor always returned a fresh one. Any site that compares wrappers with ==, uses one as a synchronization monitor, or stores one in an IdentityHashMap changes behaviour. The recipe must leave such a site untouched and report it instead of converting it.

patterns.reason: primitive wrapper constructor; deprecated for removal by JEP 390 in JDK 16, replace with the valueOf factory

verification_hint: Recompiling on jade-ant:17 with -Xlint:removal -Xmaxwarns 100000 reports zero '[removal] ... in Boolean/Integer/Long/Double/Float/Character has been deprecated and marked for removal' warnings, down from 144. All consumers still PASS.

name: java.applet.Applet deprecated for removal in JDK 17
description: JEP 398 (JDK 17) deprecates java.applet.Applet, AppletStub, AppletContext, AudioClip, javax.swing.JApplet and java.beans.AppletInitializer for removal, on the grounds that browser vendors have dropped the Java plug-in. JADE carries an applet entry point (jade.AppletBoot) and an applet-hosted DF GUI client (jade.tools.applet). Compiling on JDK 17 produces four [removal] warnings for Applet; the code still compiles and the classes still load, so nothing is broken today. What the rule records is that this subtree has no supported deployment target left and is on the removal list for a future release.

blast_class_evidence.reason: Two of the sites are 'extends Applet' on public classes and two are a field type and a constructor parameter type. Removing the Applet dependency changes the supertype of AppletBoot and DFApplet and the declared type of DFAppletCommunicator's field and constructor parameter, so every caller and subclass has to move with it.

witnesses.code: public class AppletBoot extends Applet implements Runnable {
witnesses.note: supertype; init()/destroy() are Applet lifecycle overrides and getCodeBase()/getParameter() are inherited Applet methods
supertype; its init() constructs DFAppletCommunicator(this), so the two classes have to change together
public constructor parameter type; also the field 'private Applet a;' at line 58

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: Deleting the applet subtree is a product decision, not a compiler one: jade.tools.dfgui.DFGUI and the DFAppletOntology in jade.domain are wired to it, and jade/tools/applet/DFapplet.html is a shipped artifact. The recipe must present the dependency set and stop rather than delete on its own authority.

patterns.reason: java.applet import, or a bare Applet type in a supertype / field / parameter position; revision 1 matched the bare token anywhere and caught 10 javadoc mentions of the 'DF-Applet' ontology, so revision 2 requires a type position

verification_hint: Recompiling on jade-ant:17 with -Xlint:removal reports zero '[removal] Applet in java.applet' warnings, down from four, and no .java file imports java.applet. The build still exits 0 and all consumers PASS.

name: MulticastSocket.joinGroup(InetAddress)/leaveGroup(InetAddress) deprecated in JDK 17
description: JDK 17 (JDK-8237352) added joinGroup/leaveGroup to java.net.DatagramSocket and states that the MulticastSocket API 'works as before, although most of its methods are deprecated'. JADE's main-container discovery listener joins and leaves the multicast group through the two deprecated InetAddress overloads. Behaviour on 17 is unchanged -- this is a plain deprecation, not a removal and not a semantic change -- so the rule is LOW.

blast_class_evidence.reason: Both calls are statements inside methods of MulticastMainDetectionListener, on a private MulticastSocket field. The replacement overload takes a SocketAddress and a NetworkInterface; the field type and both enclosing method signatures stay as they are.

witnesses.note: inside the constructor's setup block; 'socket' is the private MulticastSocket field declared at line 28
inside stop(); paired with the joinGroup above, so the two must move together

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: joinGroup(SocketAddress, NetworkInterface) needs an interface argument where the deprecated overload used the system default. Passing null preserves today's behaviour; naming a specific interface is a deployment decision and the recipe must not invent one.

patterns.reason: deprecated MulticastSocket.joinGroup/leaveGroup(InetAddress) overload; JDK 17 moved multicast onto DatagramSocket

verification_hint: Recompiling on jade-ant:17 reports no '[deprecation] joinGroup(InetAddress)' or 'leaveGroup(InetAddress) in MulticastSocket' warnings. A two-container JADE platform still discovers its main container over multicast.

name: ThreadGroup.destroy() terminally deprecated in JDK 16
description: JDK 16 terminally deprecated ThreadGroup.stop, destroy, isDestroyed, setDaemon and isDaemon, stating that the API and mechanism for destroying a ThreadGroup is inherently flawed and will be removed in a future release. jade.core.Runtime calls destroy() on its time-critical ThreadGroup during shutdown, inside a try/catch that already tolerates IllegalThreadStateException and a finally that nulls the field. On JDK 17 the call still works, so nothing is broken today; the fix is to drop the call and keep the field reset, which is what the JDK's own guidance amounts to. The pattern is receiver-enumerated rather than general: 'x.destroy()' cannot be resolved to ThreadGroup by a line-based scanner, and the untyped form scored 0.33 against the 0.7 gate.

blast_class_evidence.reason: One statement inside jade.core.Runtime's shutdown path. The enclosing try/catch/finally already handles the failure case and the finally clause performs the only effect that matters (criticalThreads = null), so removing the statement changes no declaration and no caller.

witnesses.note: javac on JDK 17 flags exactly this line: '[removal] destroy() in ThreadGroup has been deprecated and marked for removal'
the receiver's declared type -- this is what separates the site from the two Applet.destroy() calls in DFAppletCommunicator

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: The catch branch logs 'Time-critical threads still active' and calls criticalThreads.list(). If that diagnostic is relied on operationally, removing destroy() removes the only thing that triggers it; the recipe must keep the log or report the loss rather than silently drop it.

patterns.reason: terminally deprecated ThreadGroup member invoked on one of the workspace's own ThreadGroup-typed fields (FullResourceManager.java:39-42, Runtime.java:73). Revision 1 was the untyped '\.destroy\(\)' and caught two java.applet.Applet.destroy() calls; a line-based regex cannot resolve the receiver's type, so revision 2 enumerates the ThreadGroup-typed receivers actually declared in this tree. The limitation is deliberate and recorded: a ThreadGroup held in a differently named variable would not be flagged, which is why the verification hint checks with javac rather than with this regex

verification_hint: Recompiling on jade-ant:17 with -Xlint:removal reports no '[removal] destroy() in ThreadGroup' warning. A JADE container still shuts down cleanly and all consumers PASS.
